Error analysis and root cause mapping
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-30
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (Redwood Product), Priya Rao (Amberlane CTO), Liam O'Neill (Amberlane SRE), Sofia Martinez (Amberlane DevOps)

00:00 Maya (AE): all right hi everyone thanks for making time, i'll keep this tight we want to show the debug lab flow in the console and how traces stitch to request logs. is this still the right set of people?
00:12 Priya (CTO): yeah this is good, thanks maya. we invited liam and sofia because they're the ones who will run the bench with you. quick context: we're running inference on GCP, k8s, about 1k qps during peak, and we have a mix of in-house models and some open-source variants. main ask is reliability and predictable latency, plus we need to validate private deployment options.
00:32 Diego (SE): great, that's perfect. i'll jump in and demo the Console — start with a failing request that you sent us sample logs for, show how trace map surfaces the downstream token latency, and then how fallback to smaller-quantized model looks.
00:48 [00:48] Sofia (DevOps): quick note, we also require KMS integration, and our compliance team wants customer-managed keys, so we'll need to see the private flow for that.
01:02 Maya (AE): noted. we'll cover that in the security slide and the private deployment bit.
01:10 Diego (SE): ok pulling up the Console — upper left is the Trace Inspector, we have this request timeline on the right. here's a sample failing request — you'll see an elevated token stall at 0.9s per token, that's where the KV cache miss cascades.
01:28 Liam (SRE): when you say KV cache miss, is that the remote cache hit or our local LRU? we run a small prefix cache in front.
01:36 Diego (SE): good question. in this case the trace shows a miss in the LRU local cache, then a remote fetch added 400ms. the console shows the cache span as a subgraph node — the label was a bit noisy in the auto transcript earlier, it's "K-V cash" sometimes in the transcription.
01:52 Maya (AE): (laughs) yeah auto captions love that one.
01:56 Diego (SE): moving on — you can click into the token flame view, which rolls up per-token latencies. we can overlay model variant, quantization profile, and hardware backend. here the jump corresponds to an attention kernel selection change — which our profiler calls out.
02:20 Priya (CTO): is that kernel swap something we control? or is it the runtime automatically choosing a different kernel when sequence length grows?
02:30 Diego (SE): runtime picks optimized kernels based on active sequence length distribution and CPU/GPU type. customers can pin kernel policy if they want deterministic performance, but usually we let the runtime pick for cost/latency tradeoffs.
02:46 Aisha (Product): also note our Optimize recommendations — if we detect repeated stalls on long prefixes we suggest a caching/batching tweak and a quantization profile that keeps quality while cutting 35% token time on that path.
03:02 Liam (SRE): quality regression is our top worry. how do you validate that the quantized variant doesn't deviate on our test prompts?
03:12 Aisha (Product): we run prompt-based evals tied to customers' test sets — in the console you can attach a prompt suite and see quality diffs and regression alerts. we also version model variants so you can rollback.
03:30 Diego (SE): demoing error correlation now — the console stitches app logs (they came from your sample) to the request trace. you'll see a 503 in the app layer at 00:14 of the request timeline; hovering shows the paired stack trace and the exact model call that timed out.
03:50 [03:50] Sofia (DevOps): i see that — the stack shows a socket timeout when calling the runtime. is the timeout coming from our client library or from Redwood's backend?
04:00 Diego (SE): in that trace it maps to the runtime request queue — we show enqueued latency and dispatch latency, so you can separate client-side timeouts vs server-side throttling.
04:12 Priya (CTO): do you preserve PII in those logs? our compliance folks will insist on redaction or log residency.
04:20 Maya (AE): good point. by default hosted logs are retained in Redwood's control plane but we have private deployment options where logs live in customer VPC and you can configure retention, anonymization, or disable storage.
04:34 Liam (SRE): for private, do you support customer-managed KMS and bring-your-own-key?
04:40 Maya (AE): yes, BYOK via KMS/HSM is supported in Private mode and in Dedicated we can arrange customer-managed keys for model artifacts and request logs. we'll include the KMS integration guide in the packet.
04:54 Diego (SE): switching to fallback behavior — in the Console we have a policy simulator. i'll trigger a scenario where the primary model is overloaded and request is routed to a cheaper 8-bit quantized fallback.
05:08 [05:08] Diego (SE): you can see the routing decision in the smart routing pane: policy matched "latency_slo_violation" so it fell back. trace shows slight drop in token time but a small delta in output length — the diffs are surfaced in the structured output comparator.
05:26 Priya (CTO): how do we measure user-visible quality impact? we need an SLO that combines latency and n-gram fidelity for our QA prompts.
05:34 Aisha (Product): you can define composite SLOs in Console — e.g., p95 latency < 350ms and Rouge-L change < 2% — alerts fire when either dimension drifts.
05:50 Sofia (DevOps): ok, practical — we run in GCP us-central, any issues with region-to-region fallbacks? we need to ensure data residency for eu-bound requests.
06:02 Diego (SE): region routing is policy-driven. you can pin workload to a region or prefer low-latency region with fallback to cross-region only if you opt in. for regulated EU traffic we recommend Private with local control plane inside the region.
06:18 Maya (AE): quick qualification: what's your timeline for POC and what success looks like?
06:24 Priya (CTO): we'd like a 6-week POC. success means p95 latency improvement vs current stack by 20% or cost per inference equal/lower, and private deployment option validated for KMS and audit logs.
06:36 Maya (AE): great, that's aligned with our standard Dedicated trial. we'll provision reserved nodes to match your peak profile for benching.
06:42 [06:42] Diego (SE): back to the Trace Inspector — here's a slightly messy transcript of what the console shows, sometimes names are off in the automated captions, but the trace IDs are stable. you can export traces as newline-delimited JSON or as a zipped trace package for offline analysis.
06:58 Liam (SRE): do you keep request bodies in exports? we need to avoid exfiltration of sensitive prompts.
07:06 Diego (SE): exports obey your log retention and redaction settings; in Private you can redact bodies before exporting or use hashed/partial masks.
07:18 [07:18] Priya (CTO): could we run a bench against a dedicated pool with our real request mix? we want to see the failover behavior and the degrade gracefully scenarios.
07:26 Maya (AE): yes, that's exactly the next step. we'll create a Dedicated trial matched to your 1k qps profile, and run our bench harness with your sample logs. diego will own the config.
07:36 Diego (SE): i'll need a sample of your traffic histograms, common prompt lengths, and top error traces — priya said she'll share those. also, any special tokenization quirks?
07:48 Priya (CTO): we have a mix of multiline clinical notes and short chat prompts. token distribution skewed to long tails. i'll anonymize and send.
08:00 Aisha (Product): note on the Optimize tab — we can precompute cache prefixes for common prompts to reduce cold-start stalls. the audit shows potential 30% throughput gain for your long-tail.
08:14 Sofia (DevOps): curious about observability retention — how long can we retain request traces in the Console?
08:20 Diego (SE): hosted tiers default 90 days, enterprise can adjust to 365; in Private it's whatever you configure in your storage backend.
08:30 [08:30] Maya (AE): i want to highlight the runbook play we use in incidents — Console has a "trace playbook" feature that sequences the checks: 1) check model queue length, 2) inspect KV cache miss rate, 3) correlate app 5xxs, 4) simulate fallback on policy. you can clone and customize it.
08:50 Liam (SRE): that would help our on-call folks a lot. can runbooks be exported as runbooks for our pager tool?
08:56 Diego (SE): yes, we support webhooks and exported playbooks consumable by common incident systems.
09:06 [09:06] Diego (SE): demoing a full live incident reconstruction — i replay a request and show the exact timeline, with spike visualization at token 128. here's the root cause: a kernel stall on a certain attention op when sequence length crosses 512. we flagged it and recommended a quant profile change in Optimize.
09:28 Priya (CTO): if we apply the quant profile, what's rollback like if we see quality problems?
09:34 Aisha (Product): it's instant — rollouts are versioned and you can do canary then auto rollback if regression thresholds are hit.
09:44 [09:44] Sofia (DevOps): any special network egress policies for Private? we need to keep traffic inside our VPC and disable public egress.
09:52 Maya (AE): Private supports air-gapped deployments; traffic stays inside your VPC and you control egress. we'll share the topology doc.
10:00 Diego (SE): switching briefly to logs: Console correlates request IDs with your app logs if you pass x-request-id header. we also do fuzzy matching on timestamps if header isn't present but it's best to instrument.
10:16 Priya (CTO): we have request ids already — good. we'll ensure consistent propagation.
10:22 [10:22] Aisha (Product): to wrap up, i'll call out three artifacts we'll share: 1) security pack (SOC2, KMS guide), 2) trial Dedicated config and bench plan, 3) recording + trace export of today's demo.
10:36 Maya (AE): any outstanding objections or blockers?
10:40 Priya (CTO): main question is cost model for Dedicated at their scale, and how the SLAs look for p95 latency.
10:48 Maya (AE): we'll send pricing scenarios — Diego will model cost per inference for your 1k qps vs current infra and show tradeoffs for autoscaling. SLAs available on Dedicated are standard enterprise SLAs and we can review them with legal.
10:58 [10:58] Liam (SRE): last quick question — do you support custom authentication connectors? we run Okta with SAML and some internal mTLS.
11:06 Diego (SE): yes SSO via SAML/Okta for Console access, and we support mTLS for service-to-service auth. details in the security pack.
11:18 Priya (CTO): great, thanks everyone. we'll send the logs and aim to kick off the bench the week of the 12th.
11:26 Maya (AE): perfect. recap of next steps: we send security docs and recording (Maya), Diego provisions trial Dedicated and bench config, Amberlane shares logs and histograms (Priya).
11:40 [11:40] Sofia (DevOps): thanks, this was very practical and showed the exact paths our SREs would use.
11:48 Maya (AE): thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the packet and calendar invite for the bench kickoff.
11:52 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript: automatic captions introduced some small mis-words (KV cache -> K-V cash, SLA -> ess-el-ay). speaker turns occasionally overlap; timestamps are approximate every 30-90s.
